attributes.body_ja:
「わけにはいかない」は、「わけ」（意味：理由（りゆう）・原因（げんいん））と、格助詞（かくじょし）「に」、副助詞（ふくじょし）「は」、そして動詞（どうし）「行（い）く」の否定形（ていけい）「行（い）かない」を合（あ）わせてできた表現（ひょうげん）です。「(A) をすることはできない」や「(A) をしてはいけない」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

この文法（ぶんぽう）は、過去形（かこけい）ではない動詞（どうし）のあとに付（つ）きます。

「わけにはいかない」は、主（おも）に話（はな）し手（て）が何（なに）かを「してはいけない」と感（かん）じているときに使われます。しかし、場合（ばあい）によっては、それをした方（ほう）がよくても、事情（じじょう）によって「できない」ことを表（あらわ）すこともあります。これは話（はな）し手（て）の声（こえ）のトーンや文脈（ぶんみゃく）によって変（か）わります。

この文法（ぶんぽう）は、「そうするしかない」という、諦（あきら）めや後悔（こうかい）の気持（きも）ちを含（ふく）んで使（つか）われることもあります。
attributes.body:
わけにはいかない is a statement that combines わけ 'to be so', 'reason', or 'cause', with the case marking particle に, the adverbial particle は, and the 'cannot go' meaning of 行（い）かない. It can be translated as 'cannot afford to (A)', or 'impossible to (A)'. However, the literal meaning is much closer to 'it cannot be so that (A)'.

This structure will be used directly after the non-past form of verbs, in order to highlight them as being either highly undesirable, or highly unattainable.

Although わけにはいかない primarily highlights things that are undesirable, it may also highlight something that is desirable, but impossible for some reason. This will depend largely on the speaker's tone of voice, and context of the conversation.

In these types of sentences, the expression is quite similar to the 'I guess it's just not meant to be so' nuance that can be conveyed in English, highlighting regret.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: How to use わけ？ All uses of わけ explained in one place.
The various uses of わけ
The difference between 「いけない」 and 「いかない」
接続・意味・使い方・例文

attributes.body: Both express inability to do something, but differ in tone and usage. わけにはいかない follows the non-past form of a verb and implies a moral or social reason for being unable to act, e.g. 約束を破るわけにはいかない 'I can't break my promise.' かねる attaches to the verb stem and is more formal, often used in business settings for polite refusals or hesitations, e.g. 私には分かりかねます 'I'm afraid I'm not sure.'

first_relatable.title: わけにはいかない
first_relatable.meaning: Cannot afford to, No way, Impossible to do

second_relatable.title: かねる
second_relatable.meaning: Cannot, Be unable to, Hard to, Hesitant to

attributes.body: These express internal conflict, but from opposite angles. わけにはいかない implies being unable to act due to duty or social constraint, e.g. 断るわけにはいかない 'I just can't refuse.' ずにはいられない expresses an inability to stop oneself from acting, e.g. 笑わずにはいられない 'I couldn't help but laugh.'

first_relatable.meaning: Cannot afford to, No way, Impossible to do

second_relatable.title: ずにはいられない
second_relatable.meaning: Cannot help doing something, Cannot resist doing something

attributes.body: These are opposites in meaning. わけにはいかない expresses an inability to do something, often out of obligation or social pressure, e.g. 行きたくないけど、断るわけにはいかない 'I don't want to go, but I can't refuse.' ないわけにはいかない means the opposite: 'I have no choice but to (A),' e.g. 助けないわけにはいかない 'I can't not help them.'

attributes.body: Both express that an action cannot be avoided for similar but slightly different reasons. ずにはすまない means ‘cannot avoid doing’ due to moral obligation, responsibility, or consequences, often implying inner pressure or remorse, as in 迷惑をかけた以上、謝らずにはすまない ('Since I caused trouble, I can’t avoid apologizing.'). わけにはいかない also means ‘cannot do,’ but focuses on social rules, common sense, or one’s position making the action inappropriate, rather than moral necessity, as in 今日は大事な会議があるから休むわけにはいかない ('I can’t take the day off because there is an important meeting.').

second_relatable.title: わけにはいかない
second_relatable.meaning: Cannot afford to, No way, Impossible to do

attributes.body: Both express that an action can't be taken, but for different reasons. わけにはいかない implies restraint due to strong internal or societal reasons, e.g. 泣くわけにはいかない 'I can't very well cry.' てはいられない conveys urgency or pressure, suggesting that one can't allow a situation to continue, e.g. 怠けてはいられない 'I can't afford to slack off.'
